title: config.json — delivery-owned keys
description: The four top-level keys the delivery engine owns in .devbook/config.json — bindings, extensions, policy, gates — and `id`, which names the repository so a machine can find its overlay for it. Other components own their own entry under `components` and are not described here.

id.title: a repository id — lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens
id.description: Names this repository across every clone and worktree of it. A machine keeps its own overlay for this repository under repos/<id>/ in its devbook config directory, so the key must be a folder name; it configures nothing else. Absent, no per-repository machine overlay is looked up.

delivery.tracker.description: The work-item system this repository tracks work in. null means deliberately unbound: flows run to their file artifacts and open, comment on, and transition nothing.

delivery.roles.description: Which plugin fills each specialist role. null means deliberately unbound; an absent key means nobody has decided yet. A role is never a plugin dependency.

delivery.slots.description: Host slot bindings. Nothing binds a slot unless a repository does; an unset slot takes its documented unbound default.

delivery.mcp.description: Which MCP servers each flow extension point uses, by the server id the repository's own MCP configuration declares. A stage resolves the servers of the point it serves from the live tool list; a server that does not answer costs that stage its grounding, never the run. An absent point takes the engine default; null means deliberately none. A server is never a plugin dependency.

extensions.description: What runs at each flow extension point. The point set is closed and declared by the engine; a repository fills points, never invents them.

policy.description: Closed-enum switches over behaviour the engine already implements. Every key has a documented default, so an absent key means the engine's own choice. An unknown key is rejected, not ignored.

commit.at.description: Where the flow commits its change set. `gate` makes Personal Validation the single commit point — one commit per handback, a new commit per revise round, and no intermediate commits. `manual` leaves committing to the user.

pr.base.title: a well-formed git ref name
pr.base.description: The branch a pull request opens against. Checked here for the shape of a git ref name only — git-check-ref-format's rules, so free prose is rejected; whether the ref exists is resolved against the remote at flow time, by the stages that use it — Update Base fetches it, the pull-request lane opens against it.

gates.description: Extra human checkpoints. Configuration may add a gate anywhere; it may never remove the mandatory Personal Validation gate or hand a gate to a plugin.

mcpServerId.description: A server id as the repository's own MCP configuration spells it. Resolved from the live tool list by pattern, since a host may namespace it.

mcpServers.description: The servers a point uses, in preference order, or null for deliberately none.

roleBinding.description: A plugin or plugin:skill id, or null for deliberately unbound.

providerId.description: plugin:skill, a bare plugin resolved through its role, or repo:<skill> for a repo-native skill.

servicePoint.description: Exactly one provider. A string, or an object whose `provider` names it and whose other keys are options that provider understands.

chorePoint.description: Zero or more chores, run in declared order. `on-failure` defaults to advisory.
